details:
**Governor of California**
Newsom, a Democrat, has been governor of California since 2019 and governs from Sacramento. This is the main giveaway.

**September 2021 recall election**
A special election in which California voters were asked whether to remove Newsom from office early. Newsom easily survived it, defeating all of the replacement candidates.

**Larry Elder**
A conservative talk radio host who was the leading Republican replacement candidate in the 2021 recall and won the most votes among the replacement candidates.

**Kevin Paffrath**
A YouTuber who makes videos about real estate and finance, and the best-known Democrat running as a replacement candidate in the 2021 recall.

**The French Laundry**
A famous restaurant in Yountville in Napa Valley. In November 2020, Newsom attended a lobbyist's birthday dinner there that broke his own COVID-19 rules on gatherings, causing a scandal that helped fuel the recall effort.

**John Cox**
A Republican businessman whom Newsom defeated in the 2018 governor's race. Cox ran again in the 2021 recall and brought a live bear to campaign events to contrast himself, the "beast," with Newsom, whom he called a "pretty boy."

**Project Roomkey**
A program Newsom launched early in the COVID-19 pandemic that used state and federal money to put homeless people at high risk from the virus into hotel and motel rooms.

**SB 9**
A housing law Newsom signed in September 2021 that lets owners build duplexes on, or split, lots that had been zoned only for single-family homes. It was meant to ease California's housing shortage.

**Statewide stay-at-home order**
In March 2020, Newsom issued the first statewide COVID-19 stay-at-home order in the United States, making him a national figure in the pandemic response.

**Mayor of San Francisco**
Before becoming governor, Newsom was mayor of San Francisco. In 2004 he drew national attention by directing the city to issue marriage licenses to same-sex couples.
